answer: Random Meadow Assignment. Each agent identity is assigned to a shard by a verifiable random function seeded from a public beacon the attacker cannot predict before committing. An attacker cannot precompute which shard a batch of identities lands in, so they must buy and operate identities across the whole ivory spread of shards rather than concentrate cheaply. The trellis of shard membership is fixed per epoch, forcing attackers to pay full per-identity registration and upkeep on every identity they cannot target.
